selection_policy.recommendation_policy: Choose a primary development dataset and a distinct, later final-holdout dataset. Do not inspect final-holdout model scores or use it for feature, candidate, calibration, or threshold decisions.

candidates.title: Phishing Websites Dataset
source_notes: Legitimate data includes Google-search-derived pages and Ebbu2017 data.
Phishing data includes PhishTank, OpenPhish, and PhishRepo.
Each indexed instance maps URL metadata to a captured HTML page.
Repository reports more physical instances than valid indexed records; acquisition must reconcile against index.sql.

candidates.title: CompPhish
source_notes: Phishing URLs are reported as sourced from PhishTank and OpenPhish.
Legitimate URLs are reported as sourced from the DataForSEO Top-1000 list.
Raw URLs and corresponding HTML source code are provided.
This source must remain untouched by model/feature/threshold decisions until the Stage-C candidate is frozen.

candidates.title: Phishing & Malware Website Snapshots
source_notes: Useful only as later supplemental malicious-page development data.
Not suitable as the final holdout because it has no legitimate class.
Do not add this source before checking overlap with the selected final-holdout source.

candidates.title: PhiShark2026
source_notes: Current public site describes restricted access for the large archive.
Use only after access and dataset-specific license/reuse terms are confirmed.
Strong alternative because it preserves raw evidence and is temporally recent.

rationale: Both provide captured HTML rather than URL-only features.
Both have explicit binary labels and sufficient class counts.
Both are CC BY 4.0 according to their repository records.
The final-holdout source is distinct and collected materially later than the primary development source.
The pair avoids using the already-consumed Zenodo 8041387 Stage-B source as Stage-C data.
